meta.title: Ep 3 Hội An Vietnam , Lantern City, Must visit city of Vietnam, Things to do in Hoi an - Vietnam
meta.description:
Hoi An is an ancient town located in central vietnam, known for its well-preserved architecture, vibrant lantern-lit streets and rich cultural heritage. A UNESCO World Heritage site, it features a blend of Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese, and French influences, evident in its historic buildings, temples, and iconic Japanese Covered Bridge.

We took a flight from Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat International Airport) to Da Nang International Airport, the nearest airport to Hoi An.

District 1 (Ho chi minh city) where we were staying, It was about 8 Km to the Airport. 

This journey from Ho Chi Minh City to Da Nang we have recorded in Harish Bali Travels which will be coming on this wednesday 28th May 2025

One can also take a train from Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon Railway Station) to Da Nang Railway Station. Which will take about 17 to 20 hours.  

We started our journey from South Vietnam, this is the 3rd episode of our Vietnam series, 

In case you haven't watched the previous episodes of Vietnam, here is the link of playlist

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxHSKe-bOElw9DVfzDTNPDyDd3aICK4Ld 

Spices website link - https://spice2nuts.com/

Gadgets we use for Visa2explore & Harish Bali Travels.
Sony A 7 111 camera: https://amzn.to/4clE2zI
Z -90 Sony: https://amzn.to/3SO8T10
Go pro Hero 12: https://amzn.to/46GULw6
IPhone 15 Pro: https://amzn.to/3YJgr8Y

For Background Music, we use “Epidemic Sound” in our videos. You can use it from the link below.

https://www.epidemicsound.com/referral/ujnsd6

Date of Journey - 7th April 2025

As our flight got delayed until we reached Hoi An at 5pm, we had very less time to explore.

Coconut Boat Ride -  Thu Bon River this place is about 5 km from
Boat Ride Charges
2,45,000 VND
Rs 800 (INR) (Approx) for 1 hour 


After the Boat Ride we proceeded to Hoi An.

Hội Quán Phước Kiến -  This was a Assembly Hall established by the Chinese immigrants


Entry ticket - 1,20,000 VND
 Rs 400 INR (Approx)

Museum - While exploring the city we visited a museum where we saw Chinese immigrant merchant house, their warehouse.

Local Coffee Shop - Near the bank of Hoai River, I tried the coffee while looking at the boat and the surrounding.
Coffee - 49,000 VND
Rs 170 INR Approx


Lantern Street - There you will see a lot colorful lantern all around.

Japanese Bridge - Overall in hoi an you will the influence of Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, here we saw a bridge was started in 1617 & it was completed in 1620. There is also a Japanese temple on the bridge.

Boating - We did the boating, generally the boat ride cost is around $10 to $15 which is Rs 1000 to Rs 1200 approx. The boating we did on the Hoai River which is a tributary of the Thu Bon River, flowing gently through the heart of Hoi An.

Bài Chòi - When we were crossing the bridge, we noticed the locals were playing this game, it is traditional Vietnamese folk art and game that combines music, poetry, and storytelling.

Maazi - We had dinner at indian restaurant, we ordered Dal Makhani 1,30,000 VND  in Rs 425 INR Approx and Tawa Roti - 35000 VND in Rs 125 INR Approx

After that we went to our hotel.

Hope you liked the video.

comments.author: @visa2explore
comments.text:
Harish Bali this side, looking at comments i spotted this trail, so thought to write a comment here... I agree with your thoughts on this subject. 

We are mostly running short of time bcoz things on the ground are not as easy at it seems, so much of time gets consumed in taking permission for making video at respective place. This is background of the food. My team does not prefer local food unless i push them to have it in lunch or dinner. 

I try to motivate them but if they say they want to have indian food then, no second time asking, i go with them to indian food restaurant. When you go to any restaurant it takes times , if after they are done with their food, i decide that i want to go to local food eatery then you lose your time badly.....This is one reason.

Most youtubers travel on their own  without any team, which somehow i can't do, my dependence is on them for video shoot, so i have to be 100% flexible when it comes to food choice preference. Plus they are pure veg, don't even eat egg.... so we decided that atleast one meal of the day we will have in Indian food. Now the option which is left is shoot or ignore.. 

if i had cut this indian food option from the video, then there would be no trail here, that's how things are....Most of us generally pin point what we don't like in a particular video and in many cases miss to mention what was good or alteast  better then many other videos available online on that very subject.

My personal preference is so much towards local food and culture that learning about it and sharing through video is my first preference but sometimes bcoz of reasons beyond control, things are not always aligned to the objective, despite best efforts.

Rest all good, BTW - Central Vietnam is the most beautiful place of Vietnam. Bye for now.
